intro: Pine Lodge Addiction Recovery is a 42 day inpatient addiction treatment centre in North Central Regina, accredited through Accreditation Canada. Its counsellors work from a client centred, trauma informed model and build each person's case plan and relapse prevention plan around the supports waiting at home.

Clients arrive by referral, usually straight from detox, since Pine Lodge has no detox of its own. Once the inpatient program ends, a second-stage post-treatment program offers counselling groups, one-to-one sessions and short-term supportive housing in Regina.

pillars.title: Forty Two Days With a Plan for Home
pillars.body: Pine Lodge's inpatient program lasts 42 days. Counsellors write an individual case plan and a full relapse prevention plan with each client, built on the resources that person will have outside the centre and in their home community. Pine Lodge sees inpatient treatment as one part of a longer chain of care, so planning for the day someone leaves starts early. It also works with community organizations in Regina to keep people supported after they go.

pillars.title: A Renovated Home in North Central Regina
pillars.body: Pine Lodge used to be in Indian Head. A fire on Christmas Eve 2020 stopped operations for nearly two years, and in October 2022 the centre reopened in a fully renovated brick building at 3535 8th Avenue in North Central Regina. The original Pine Lodge sign made the move too and now stands in the courtyard. The centre is on Treaty 4 territory and has a cultural program counsellor on its team.

pillars.title: Second-Stage Support and Recovery Housing
pillars.body: The post-treatment program is for adults who recently finished an addiction program and need help with the next step. It runs half-day counselling groups and one-to-one sessions with post house counsellors. Separately, Pine Lodge offers short-term supportive housing, now 25 beds, with recovery support workers on hand. Residents are expected to stay sober and to work toward school, a job and a place of their own.

overviewH2: Pine Lodge Addiction Recovery: Centre Overview
overview: Pine Lodge says everyone with a substance use disorder deserves barrier free, quality inpatient treatment, and it ties its work to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's calls to action. In 2022 it adopted model standards of care based on British Columbia's provincial standards for adult residential substance use services, and those standards shape its residential program.

Its beds have long had provincial support: a 2019 Government of Saskatchewan release funded 10 more inpatient beds for a total of 33, and since February 2026 the Saskatchewan Health Authority funds 16 sober living spaces in two Pine Lodge homes at $863,000 a year. In August 2026, MBC News described Pine Lodge as a non-profit charity funded by the Saskatchewan Health Authority, with 38 inpatient beds. Call the intake line to confirm whether any cost applies to you.

location.heading: Pine Lodge Addiction Recovery in Regina, Saskatchewan
location.intro: Pine Lodge is on 8th Avenue in North Central Regina, a short drive from downtown. Moose Jaw and Indian Head are each about 45 minutes away, Lumsden roughly 30 minutes, and Saskatoon around two and a half hours north on Highway 11.

faqIntro: Answers come from the Pine Lodge website, the Government of Saskatchewan and news reports. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How long is treatment at Pine Lodge?
faqs.a: The inpatient program is 42 days. People who finish can then apply to Pine Lodge's post-treatment program, which adds group and one-to-one counselling and short-term supportive housing.

faqs.q: Is Pine Lodge funded by the Saskatchewan Health Authority or private?
faqs.a: Pine Lodge does not publish a client fee, and its beds have had public funding. The province paid for 10 more inpatient beds in 2019, bringing Pine Lodge to 33, and in 2026 the Saskatchewan Health Authority signed an agreement to fund 16 of its sober living spaces at $863,000 a year. In August 2026, MBC News described Pine Lodge as a non-profit charity funded by the Saskatchewan Health Authority, with 38 inpatient beds. Ask the intake line whether any cost applies to you.

faqs.q: How do I get a referral to Pine Lodge?
faqs.a: Download the referral package from the Inpatient Treatment page of the Pine Lodge website. It has a referral form and a medical form, and it is usually completed with an addictions counsellor or other referring worker. Questions go to the intake line at 306-510-1893.
No. Pine Lodge expects clients to come straight from a detox program into treatment, and its referral form is built around that handover. Arrange detox first, then the referral.
Yes. Pine Lodge says it is accredited through Accreditation Canada, and the seal on its website reads Accredited with Commendation.

faqs.q: What happens after the 42 day program?
faqs.a: Pine Lodge runs a second-stage post-treatment program. It offers half-day counselling groups, one-to-one sessions with post house counsellors, and short-term supportive housing with recovery support workers. Participants are expected to stay sober, take part in programming and work toward education, a job and housing in their community.

faqs.q: Who can join the post-treatment program?
faqs.a: Adults 18 and older who recently completed an addiction recovery program and need transitional support. Most come from Pine Lodge's own inpatient program, but group and one-to-one sessions are also open as outpatient services. Contact intake@pinelodgerecovery.ca for referral details.

faqs.q: Where is Pine Lodge and how do I get there?
faqs.a: Pine Lodge is at 3535 8th Avenue in North Central Regina. It is about 45 minutes from Moose Jaw and Indian Head, roughly 30 minutes from Lumsden and about two and a half hours from Saskatoon by car.

faqs.q: What is Pine Lodge's approach to treatment?
faqs.a: Care is client centred and trauma informed. Each client builds an individual case plan and a relapse prevention plan with a counsellor, using resources available in their home community, and Pine Lodge follows model standards of care adopted in 2022.
Pine Lodge Addiction Recovery Inc. is led by executive director Andrew Love and governed by a board of directors. It also accepts donations through its website.
